name: landlock_add_rule
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_landlock_add_rule, int ruleset_fd, enum landlock_rule_type rule_type, const void *rule_attr, uint32_t flags);
description: The landlock_add_rule() system call adds a new Landlock rule to an existing ruleset. A rule describes an action on an object, such as a file hierarchy with specific access rights. It is used to enforce security restrictions on filesystem operations.

parameters.name: ruleset_fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the Landlock ruleset obtained from landlock_create_ruleset(2).

parameters.name: rule_type
parameters.description: Identifies the type of the rule, such as LANDLOCK_RULE_PATH_BENEATH for file hierarchies.

parameters.name: rule_attr
parameters.description: Pointer to the rule attributes structure, which varies based on rule_type.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Must be set to 0; any other value is invalid.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and sets errno

errors.description: Landlock is supported by the kernel but disabled at boot time.
Flags is not 0, or the rule accesses are inconsistent.
ruleset_fd is not a valid file descriptor, or a member of rule_attr is not.
ruleset_fd is not a ruleset file descriptor, or a member of rule_attr is not the expected type.
ruleset_fd has no write access to the underlying ruleset.
rule_attr was not a valid address.
